To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

the pediatric workforce is not large enough to meet the needs and expectations of the American public, that the current system of pediatric medical education is not producing enough pediatricians, and that the current system is not producing the right kinds of pediatricians.

(1) the health care system must be reformed to ensure access to comprehensive health care for all children and to ensure that the health care system is able to provide the care that children and their families need, (2) the education and training of all health care professionals must be reformed, and (3) the health care financing system must be restructured to ensure access, provide incentives, and provide adequate reimbursement to meet the needs identified in the first two goals.

(1) the pediatrician's role in the care of infants, children and adolescents will expand in the future; (2) pediatric education should be reorganized to meet the needs for the 21st Century; (3) a new model for the delivery of pediatric education is proposed; (4) pediatric education must be reorganized to accommodate the new model; (5) a new financing mechanism is proposed; (6) the pediatric community must be involved in implementing these changes.

the development of a model of pediatric education for the 21st Century.
